findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is optional and is now commonly represented as an empty array. Destructuring an empty array makes `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, but this condition immediately reads `.integration`. Any booking with Google Meet selected but no destination calendar will throw before the calendar/video event is created, rather than falling back to Daily as intended. Guard this access with optional chaining or treat a missing destination calendar as non-Google.

findings.title: Office 365 always uses the first host's destination calendar
findings.body: EventManager invokes this service once per destination credential for a collective event, but this implementation always selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. When processing a later host's Office 365 credential, it therefore attempts to create the event in the first host's calendar, which that credential generally cannot access, or creates it in the wrong calendar. The selected destination must be matched to the credential being used (as the Google implementation does), not array position.

findings.title: Lark collective events are written to the first host calendar for every credential
findings.body: The collective-event loop creates an event for each destination/credential, but Lark derives `calendarId` solely from the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`. A Lark credential belonging to a subsequent host will try to write to the first host's calendar and will fail authorization or place the event incorrectly. Select the destination calendar associated with the active credential instead of destructuring the first element.

findings.title: CalDAV collective events only target the first destination calendar
findings.body: For each destination credential, EventManager calls this calendar service, but event creation filters the calendars returned for that credential using only `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. Consequently, later collective hosts either have no matching calendar (so no event is created) or target the first host's URL, which is not accessible with their credentials. The target must be resolved per credential/destination rather than globally from index zero.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking loses all non-primary host destinations
findings.body: This handler reconstructs the event from the booking using only its single `destinationCalendar` relation (or the confirming user's calendar) and wraps that one item in an array. It does not load the collective event type's hosts or their destination calendars. Thus a pending/confirmation-required collective booking will create calendar references only for the primary host when confirmed, even though normal booking creation now includes all hosts. Persist/load the full destination set or rebuild it from the collective hosts before calling `handleConfirmation`.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference of each occurrence
findings.body: Inside the loop over all calendar references, the recurring branch finds a single reference with `updBooking.references.find(...)`. For a collective booking each occurrence has multiple calendar references, so only the first one is selected; the code then retries that same reference through every calendar credential and never deletes the other hosts' events. This leaves orphaned events in non-primary host calendars (and can issue deletion requests with the wrong credential). Iterate every calendar reference and use its recorded credential ID when deleting it.

findings.title: Organization slug is no longer stored when team billing is disabled
findings.body: The previous condition stored `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was false. This change reverses that behavior and omits the slug entirely in that mode. Since organization URLs and collision checks use the slug, organizations created with team billing disabled can no longer be addressed by their requested subdomain/slug. This unrelated condition change should be reverted unless the corresponding organization routing/storage behavior was migrated.
